newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent faces first resistance at $19.64.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent faces first resistance at $19.64.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+September Brent faces first resistance up at $19.64 a barrel and then above that at around $19.90, the site of gaps on the September chart and the contiuation chart.
+Gas oil is called around four dollars higher and this brings the market into an older range with resistance up at $177.
IPE Brent crude oil futures are looking neutral to positive after Monday's sharp rise but gas oil is set to open firmer and face resistance up at $177 a tonne.
September Brent closed 51 cents a barrel firmer on Tuesday at $19.46 while August gas oil was 75 cents a tonne up at $172.25.
"There is a little resistance up at $19.64," one dealer said, referring to Monday's price peak. "And if we fall back there is not really much until we get back down to $19.00-$19.10."
These latter numbers correspond to recent highs.

Another broker said stronger resistance would appear at around $19.90. This corresponds not only to a continuation chart gap between $19.88 and $19.93, but also a larger gap on the September chart from $19.90 to $20.00.
Gas oil is expected to open higher and this will bring the market within range of $177.00, a series of three previous highs at the beginning of June, a broker said.
Above that level lies the May 22 peak on the continuation chart at $179.50.

Support for gas oil lies at $173.50. This was a previous resistance level created by a chart gap at the beginning of June, and it also corresponds to the 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of the downwards move from the May 20 peak on the August chart to the July 15 low.
An equivalent Fibonacci number on the Brent September chart would be $19.36 and this constitutes a support level.
